title: Borel summation of compactly supported matrix symbols
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and the symbol estimates of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Fix $m\geq1$, matrix dimensions $p,q\geq0$, an integer $r$, and a compact set $K\subset\mathbf R^m$. For each $j\geq0$ let $a_j:\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C^p,\mathbf C^q)$ be smooth, vanish for $x\notin K$, and satisfy, for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$, $$\sup_{x,\xi}(1+|\xi|)^{-r+j+|\beta|}\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta a_j(x,\xi)\|<\infty.$$ There is a smooth symbol $b\in S^r$ vanishing for $x\notin K$ such that for every $L\geq1$, $$b-\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}a_j\in S^{r-L}.$$ All symbol estimates here are uniform for $x\in\mathbf R^m$. No convergence of the original series is required.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.7, pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, applied entrywise with a common compact spatial support.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-bump] with center $0$ and radii $1,2$, obtaining $\beta$, and put $\theta=1-\beta$. The bump's stated support implies $\beta=0$ for $|\xi|>2$ and, by continuity, also for $|\xi|=2$. Thus $\theta=0$ on $|\xi|\leq1$ and $\theta=1$ on $|\xi|\geq2$. Use $P_{s,n}$ from [lem-sfb-symbol-dilated-cutoff-estimates]. The hypotheses give $P_{r-j,n}(a_j)<\infty$ for every $j,n$: the maximum is over finitely many multi-indices. Multiplication by a cutoff in $\xi$ preserves vanishing for $x\notin K$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3.7, printed pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read. §3.7 p.7, choice of the fixed cutoff; uniform matrix seminorms.

proof.text:
For each $j\geq1$, apply [lem-sfb-symbol-dilated-cutoff-estimates] to $a_j$, with $s=r-j$, $t=r-j+1$ and $n=j$. Choose recursively $R_j\geq\max(1,j,R_{j-1}+1)$ (omit $R_0$ at the first stage) so large that
$$C_j P_{r-j,j}(a_j)/(1+R_j)\leq2^{-j}.$$
Only finitely many constants enter this choice. Set $c_j(x,\xi)=\theta(\xi/R_j)a_j(x,\xi)$. Then $P_{r-j+1,j}(c_j)\leq2^{-j}$. The same cited estimate with $t=s=r-j$, for each $n$, gives $c_j\in S^{r-j}$. No growth restriction on the seminorms of the original sequence was assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3.7, printed pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read. §3.7 pp.7–8, choose inverse cutoff scales sufficiently small; diagonal choice of radii.

proof.text:
Define the actual function
$$b(x,\xi)=a_0(x,\xi)+\sum_{j\geq1}^{\mathrm{fin}}c_j(x,\xi).$$
This sum is locally finite: around $(x_0,\xi_0)$ choose a bounded frequency neighborhood $|\xi|<M$; every $j>M$ has $R_j\geq j>M$ and hence $c_j=0$ throughout it. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-finite-smooth-sum] to these smooth functions on $\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m$ with values in the finite-dimensional real normed space of complex matrices. It gives smoothness, and $b=0$ for $x\notin K$ since each summand is zero there. On this same neighborhood $b$ is a finite sum, so every mixed partial derivative is the corresponding finite sum of derivatives. This is differentiation of a finite local identity, with no exchange of infinite limits.

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3.7, printed pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read. §3.7 pp.7–8, definition and smoothness of the cutoff sum; local-finiteness implementation.

proof.text:
Fix $L\geq1$. Subtracting the first $L$ original symbols from the local finite expression gives
$$b-\sum_{j<L}a_j=\sum_{1\leq j<L}(\theta(\xi/R_j)-1)a_j+\sum_{j\geq L}^{\mathrm{fin}}c_j.$$
Each term in the first sum is $-\beta(\xi/R_j)a_j$, with frequency support in $|\xi|\leq2R_j$. All its derivatives are bounded uniformly in $x$: the given derivative estimates for $a_j$ are bounded on this frequency ball, and the finitely many derivatives of the fixed smooth scaled bump are bounded there. For any integer $t$, $(1+|\xi|)^{-t+|\beta|}$ is bounded on that ball as well. Thus each such term is in every $S^t$, in particular $S^{r-L}$. When $L=1$ the first sum is empty.

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3.7, printed pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read. §3.7 p.8, finite correction terms with bounded frequency support; elementary seminorm verification.

proof.text:
For the tail in step 4 fix multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$, put $n=\max(|\alpha|,|\beta|)$ and $J=\max(L+1,n)$. If $j\geq J$, then $r-j+1\leq r-L$, $n\leq j$, and the estimate of step 2 gives
$$(1+|\xi|)^{-r+L+|\beta|}\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta c_j(x,\xi)\|\leq P_{r-j+1,j}(c_j)\leq2^{-j}.$$
At any point only finitely many derivatives in the tail can be nonzero, by the neighborhood argument of step 3. The triangle inequality bounds the weighted norm of their sum by the corresponding finite sum of $2^{-j}$, hence by $2$ (the finite geometric-sum formula). The finitely many remaining indices $L\leq j<J$ have $c_j\in S^{r-j}\subseteq S^{r-L}$ by step 2 and $1+|\xi|\geq1$. Consequently the whole tail has every defining seminorm of $S^{r-L}$ finite, uniformly for all $x,\xi$.

The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read. §3.7 p.8, tail bound for every remainder order; explicit finite geometric bound.

proof.text: Steps 4–5 and the triangle inequality show $b-\sum_{j<L}a_j\in S^{r-L}$ for every $L\geq1$. Taking $L=1$ yields $b-a_0\in S^{r-1}\subseteq S^r$, whence $b\in S^r$ because $a_0\in S^r$. Step 3 already gives smoothness and the prescribed spatial support. The one sequence of radii chosen in step 2 works for all derivative indices and all $L$; the construction never sums the unmodified series.
